newsitem.title: UK: South African gold price to climb-Morgan Grenfell.
newsitem.headline: South African gold price to climb-Morgan Grenfell.

text.p: Spot gold should hit $400 per ounce this year and the South African bullion price a minimum of 1,833 rand per ounce by year end, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
"The dollar gold price has little downside currently and should continue to rise reflecting continued supply/demand tightness," the stockbroker said in a report on South African gold shares.
Spot gold fixed at $386.55 on Monday afternoon.
"The rand gold price is also set to continue reaching new highs with the rand expected to depreciate against the dollar to 4.80 by year end," it added.
The forecast of a 1,833 rand gold price by December 1996 compares with a price on Monday of around 1,730 rand.
Forward sales and and central bank disposals will not be sufficient to fill the gap between primary demand and supply, the report said.
"If disinvestment becomes investment, the price will have to rise," it said.

Any gold sales by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to finance debt relief to poor nations would attack sentiment, but Germany might be able to gather enough opposition to head off the planned liquidation of a small portion of IMF bullion stocks.

"The proposal needs a 85 percent majority. Germany, with 5.5 percent of the votes is strongly opposed, as is Switzerland (2.8 percent) and a number of other European countries are ambivalent," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
The demand side is bullish, with a good Indian monsoon and economic strength in the U.S. likely leading to strong Christmas jewellery sales.
In South Africa, supply could edge down on labour problems.
"On the supply side there is the potential for a strike in South Africa, which could see supply fall below 500 tonnes this year," the report said.
South African gold prices would get an added boost from rand weakness, increasing by 15.5 percent to 2,028 rand by June 1997.
The rand is expected to slide to 4.80 to the dollar by the end of 1996 and 5.20 by June 1997, which is expected to spark government moves to support the currency.

"...(the) government will be forced to implement "market friendly' policies in the current investment horizon. We subsequently expect the rand to appreciate to 4.75 by December 1997, implying fair value (against the dollar) once again," it said.
